observed.title: Observed traffic
observed.empty: No variant served a request in the {{window}}. Traffic appears here once the route has been called with the variants saved.
observed.note: Observed is each variant's share of the requests the variants served, counting failovers as well as first attempts, so a variant that others fail over to reads higher than its weight.
observed.noteWithFirstAttempt: Observed is each variant's share of the requests it answered, counting failovers, so a variant that others fail over to reads higher than its weight. First attempt is the share of requests answered on the first attempt, with no failover. A request first sent to one variant that failed over is logged under the variant that answered, with a reason, so it counts for neither: a variant that often fails over reads below its weight there.
observed.noteWithAssigned: Assigned is each variant's share of the requests it was dialled to first, whether it answered them or they failed over. It is not the sampled split: a variant skipped while its breaker is open or its targets are parked is dialled first by none of the requests sampled for it. Observed is its share of the requests it answered, counting failovers, and First attempt the share it answered with no failover. Requests logged before the gateway recorded the first variant count under Assigned only when they did not fail over.
observed.noteSampled: Sampled is each variant's share of the requests the weighted split picked it for, before the gateway skipped a variant whose breaker is open or whose targets are parked, so it is the share to compare with Configured. Where Sampled is above Assigned, the gateway routed requests around the variant. Requests logged before the gateway recorded the sample are not counted there. A realtime session is not sampled by weight yet: it leads with the first variant with a non-zero weight, and each of its turns counts for that variant.

pricing.editSubtitle: Prices are per million tokens (Mtok); saving upserts by model name.
pricing.modelNameInfo: The model id this price applies to, spelled as clients send it. Pick one from the list or type it. A model with no price row adds nothing to the spend figures.
pricing.cacheWriteInfo: The rate for tokens written to the provider's prompt cache: Anthropic's 5 minute cache, and any write a provider reports without a cache lifetime. Anthropic bills a write above the input rate. Leave it empty to price writes at the input rate.
pricing.cacheWrite1hInfo: The rate for tokens written to Anthropic's 1 hour prompt cache; no other provider reports this share. Anthropic bills it above the 5 minute write. Leave it empty to price those writes at the 5 minute cache-write rate, or at the input rate when that is empty too.
pricing.imageInfo: The rate for a model the provider bills per image. The count is the images the response returns, so a request for several is priced by what came back. It is added to the token price, so a model billed only per image takes 0 for the token prices above. Leave it empty if the model is billed by tokens.
pricing.audioInputPrice: Price per minute of input audio (optional)
pricing.audioInfo: The rate for a transcription or translation model billed by the minute. The minutes come from the duration the response states: ask for verbose_json, or use a model that reports its audio duration. A response that states none is recorded with unknown usage rather than as free.
pricing.speechInputPrice: Price per million characters of speech input (optional)
pricing.speechInfo: The rate for a text-to-speech model billed by the character. The count is the length of the request's input, since the audio that comes back states no length.
pricing.audioInTokenInfo: The rate for the audio tokens a realtime or audio model is sent, for a model that bills them above its text tokens. The response's usage says how many of the input tokens were audio. Leave it empty to price them at the input price above.
pricing.audioOutTokenInfo: The rate for the audio tokens the model speaks. Leave it empty to price them at the output price above.
pricing.cachedAudioPrice: Cached audio input price per Mtok (optional)
pricing.cachedAudioInfo: The rate for audio tokens served from the provider's prompt cache, for a provider that says how many of its cache hits were audio (a realtime session does). Leave it empty to price them at the cached input price, or at the audio input price when that is empty too.
pricing.currencyHint: Any code — ISO-4217, crypto, or a custom unit. Anything other than the base currency needs a rate in [currency.rates]; without one the price is rejected rather than charged at the wrong rate.
pricing.currencyInfo: Spend and budgets accumulate in the deployment's base currency. A price in another currency is converted at the configured rate before it reaches a budget.
pricing.priceRequired: Enter a price. Type 0 if the model is free; empty stays unpriced.

guardrailProviders.intro: Register as many services as you need and enable any number of them; saving one never changes another. Which requests a provider sees is decided by guardrail policies: one that policies list runs only for the requests they apply to, and an enabled provider no policy lists runs on every request no policy covers.

guardrailProviders.emptyBody: Register a self-hosted HTTP guardrail service. Credentials remain environment references, never stored secret values.
guardrailProviders.kindInfo: A webhook posts each request to an HTTP service. A local classifier runs inside every gateway from a weights file on the gateway's own file system.
guardrailProviders.modelPathHint: Absolute path of the weights file on each gateway's file system. The control plane does not read it.

guardrailProviders.dialogBody: Use an HTTP endpoint and reference credentials by environment variable. Enabling this provider adds it to the active ones without pausing any other.
guardrailProviders.nameInfo: Recorded on the request log beside this provider's outcomes, so choose a name you will recognise there.

guardrailProviders.urlInvalid: Start the URL with http:// or https://.
guardrailProviders.stageInfo: When the gateway asks this service for a decision: on the request body before it goes upstream, or on the response body before it reaches the client.
guardrailProviders.failureInfo: What happens to a request when this service times out or errors. Fail closed refuses it; fail open lets it through unchecked.
guardrailProviders.timeoutInfo: How long the gateway waits for a decision, in milliseconds. The request waits too, so keep it short; the default is 2000.
guardrailProviders.retriesInfo: Extra attempts after a connection failure, a timeout or a 5xx answer. 0 means one attempt, so a slow service costs at most one timeout.
guardrailProviders.bodyCapInfo: The most content, in bytes, sent to this service. Longer content is cut and flagged as truncated. The default is 65536 (64 KiB).
guardrailProviders.scoredBytesInfo: Total bytes the local classifier may read across overlapping windows. Leave blank for 8 times the body cap; the maximum is 16777216 (16 MiB).
guardrailProviders.scoredBytesInvalid: Enter a value from the body cap through 16777216 (16 MiB), or leave it blank.
guardrailProviders.onTruncatedInfo: What happens when text exceeds the scoring budget. Scoring what fits records semantic_truncated; refusing rejects the request before scoring.
guardrailProviders.authInfo: How the gateway identifies itself to this service. A bearer token goes in the Authorization header, a shared secret in a header of its own. The secret itself is read from an environment variable.

guardrailProviders.activateHint: Adds this provider to the active ones; no other provider is paused.

notAwaitedDetail.notification: This call was sent as a notification, so no reply was awaited. Its status is only what the server's HTTP response said, not what the tool did, and the summary leaves it out of the failure rate.
notAwaitedDetail.notificationFailed: This call was sent as a notification, so no reply was awaited. The server's HTTP response refused or failed it, so it was not delivered, and the summary counts it as a failure.
notAwaitedDetail.accepted: The server accepted this call and sends its reply on the event stream the client holds open, which is not matched back to the call. Nothing here says what the tool did, and the summary leaves it out of the failure rate.
notAwaitedDetail.unread: The gateway forwarded this request body to a server no tool group governs without reading it, because it was compressed or was not valid JSON. The tool calls it held are not itemised, so this one row stands for the whole request and the summary leaves it out of the failure rate.

mcpSettings.saveFailed: Could not save the MCP settings
mcpSettings.lead: These defaults apply to every server in the organization that has no override of its own: the proxy uses them for timeouts and retries, and for tools a server did not declare. A new server that names no transport starts on the default transport below. Authorization still comes from server scopes and each user’s OAuth session.
mcpSettings.failureModeNoEffectReason: Deprecated and ignored: the proxy refuses every request it cannot inspect for tool policy, since forwarding one unchecked could let a refused tool run.
mcpSettings.allowUnlistedHint: Permit calls to tools the server’s manifest does not declare. Off, the proxy refuses them. An organization created before manifests were enforced stays on until you save it off; a newer one starts off.
mcpSettings.persistNote: A server’s own overrides win over these values, and these win over the deployment-level timeouts.

logsSettings.captureOffSummary: Nothing is stored: no prompt or completion text is retained for any request. Log metadata — model, tokens, cost, latency, status — is unaffected and keeps flowing.
logsSettings.captureOnSummary: Stored: the raw prompt and completion body of each matching request, truncated at {{bytes}} bytes, kept for {{hours}} hours and then deleted. Redacted before writing: {{redacted}}. Models captured: {{models}}.
logsSettings.sampleRateHint: Share of requests written to the log. Lower it to cut storage on high-volume deployments. The Dashboard, LLM Logs, Business Units, Customers, Account usage and alert rules read this log. Their request counts, spend, tokens and alert signals are scaled up from the sample, so they are estimates; the LLM Logs list shows only the sampled requests. Budgets, rate limits and /metrics still count every request.

sampled.title_one: The log keeps about {{numerator}} in {{denominator}} request.
sampled.title_other: The log keeps about {{numerator}} in {{denominator}} requests.
sampled.body: Counts, spend and tokens on the screens that read it are scaled up from this sample, so they are estimates.
sampled.noneBody: The screens that read it get no new requests, spend or tokens.

logsSettings.captureHint: Store raw prompt and completion bodies alongside the log metadata. Off by default — payloads carry whatever the caller sent.
logsSettings.maxBytesHint: Anything longer is truncated. Maximum 1048576 (1 MiB).
logsSettings.redactedHint: Comma-separated JSON keys stripped from captured payloads before they are stored. Redaction happens before the write, so a redacted value never reaches storage.

redaction.detectorsHint: Scans the text of every captured string and replaces a match with a marker such as [redacted:aws_key], before the write.
redaction.patternsHint: One per line as name=regular expression. The name becomes the marker. Linear-time engine: no look-around or backreferences; at most 16 patterns of 256 bytes.
redaction.patternLine: Each line must be name=pattern, with a name of lowercase letters, digits or underscore.
redaction.previewHint: Runs the policy as edited above against a sample body. Nothing is stored or logged; the sample goes to the server only for this check.

logsSettings.onlyModelsHint: Pick from the models that carried traffic in the last 30 days, or type one that has not yet. Leave empty to capture payloads for every model.
logsSettings.onlyKeysHint: Pick from the virtual keys of the project selected in the sidebar. Leave empty to capture payloads for every key.

clientSettings.baseUrlHint: The address clients point their SDK at. Set the gateway’s own address, such as its load balancer or a custom domain.
clientSettings.forwardedHint: Inbound client headers passed through to the upstream provider, comma or newline separated. Everything not listed is dropped at the gateway.
clientSettings.injectedHint: Static headers the gateway adds to every upstream request. A trace-context header of the same name still wins, so correlation cannot be broken from here. Values are treated as deployment secrets and are never written to the audit log.
clientSettings.injectedNone: No headers injected — upstream requests carry only what the gateway and the caller already send.
clientSettings.correlationHint: Header carrying the end-to-end request id. The gateway reuses the caller’s value when present, mints one when absent, and echoes it on the response so a client can find its own call in the logs.

retries.title: Retries
retries.desc: Upstream retry budget for a single client request. Backoff grows exponentially from the base up to the cap.

timeouts.title: Timeouts
timeouts.desc: How long the gateway waits on an upstream. The request timeout covers the wait for response headers, so a stream that has started is never cut short. Zero disables the timeout.

queue.title: Admission queue
queue.desc: Each provider gets its own bounded queue and worker set, so a slow provider cannot consume the admission capacity of healthy ones.

backpressure.drop: Drop — shed the request immediately with an overload response.
backpressure.block: Block — wait for capacity until the block timeout expires.
backpressure.error: Error — return a structured queue_full error immediately.

validation.maxRetries: Max retries must be between 0 and 10.
validation.retryBase: Retry base must be between 0 and 60000 ms.
validation.retryCap: Retry cap must be between 0 and 600000 ms.

guardrailPolicies.intro: A policy pins a set of guardrail providers, score thresholds and a violation action to a scope: the whole deployment, an organization, a project, a route or a virtual key.
guardrailPolicies.precedence: Exactly one policy applies to a request: the most specific enabled one that matches it (key, then route, project, organization, deployment). It replaces the broader ones rather than merging with them, so a narrower policy must list every provider it wants. A request no policy matches is checked only by providers no policy lists, with no thresholds. Thresholds act only on the scored categories a provider returns; a provider's own block always blocks.
guardrailPolicies.emptyBody: Without a policy, every enabled provider runs on every request. Add one to scope providers to a route, project or key, or to set score thresholds.

descriptions.roundRobin: Sequential rotation through targets. For homogeneous pools and stateless workloads.
descriptions.random: Uniform random pick. For simple pools where every target is equivalent.
descriptions.powerOfTwo: The less loaded of two random targets. For requests that vary in duration.
descriptions.consistentHash: Hash ring keyed by session or prompt. For multi-turn chat, sticky sessions and KV cache reuse.
descriptions.cacheAware: Approximate prefix affinity to warm targets. For shared system prompts, few-shot examples and RAG.
descriptions.weighted: Smooth weighted round-robin by target weight. For A/B splits and capacity-based routing.
descriptions.pipeline: Filter, score, then pick the best. For blending weight, load and cache signals.
descriptions.cheapest: Lowest catalog price for the upstream model. For cost-sensitive routing across mixed-price providers.
descriptions.fastest: Lowest observed request latency. For heterogeneous pools where speed matters most.
descriptions.preciseCacheAware: Exact resident-prefix score from vLLM KV events. For vLLM fleets that publish KV events.
descriptions.lmcacheAware: Cache availability and free capacity from the LMCache controller. For LMCache-backed fleets.
descriptions.adaptive: Blend of latency, cost and load, tuned by the gateway. For pools mixed in both price and latency.
descriptions.loraAware: Prefers a target that already holds the requested LoRA adapter. For fleets serving many adapters over shared base weights.
descriptions.predictedLatency: Ranks targets by the modelled cost of this request, from queue depth and prompt size. For variable prompt sizes and deep queues.
